presentingComplaint: Fever, headache and body aches for 4 days with a spreading rash noticed today
history: Previously well farmer from a rural hill district who returned from working in scrub and cattle sheds 6 days ago. Four days of moderate continuous fever with frontal headache and diffuse myalgia. He remained ambulant, ate reasonably and self-medicated with paracetamol with partial relief. This morning he noticed small pink-red spots starting on the ankles and wrists. He recalls removing ticks from his dog and had an itchy 'insect bite' on the left flank about a week ago. No breathlessness, no bleeding, no confusion, urine output normal. No prior comorbidity, not on any regular medication.
examination: Alert, oriented, not toxic. A single 0.8 cm painless black-crusted lesion (eschar/tache noire) with a surrounding erythematous halo on the left flank, with a small non-tender inguinal node. Sparse blanching maculopapular rash over both ankles, wrists and forearms including early involvement of the palms; no petechiae, no mucosal bleeding. Chest clear, abdomen soft, no hepatosplenomegaly, no meningism, no focal neurology.
imaging: Chest radiograph normal. Abdominal ultrasound normal, no hepatosplenomegaly.
microbiology: Malaria rapid antigen and peripheral smear negative. Dengue NS1 and IgM negative. Weil-Felis OX-2/OX-19 weakly positive; Spotted Fever Group Rickettsia IgM ELISA positive; convalescent IFA seroconversion planned. Blood cultures sterile at 48h.
finalDiagnosis: Early spotted fever group rickettsiosis (Indian tick typhus, Rickettsia conorii) with eschar and acral maculopapular rash
citations: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, Rickettsial Diseases, 22e (2022)
ICMR Guidelines for Diagnosis and Management of Rickettsial Diseases (2015)
stewardship: Mild, early, outpatient-manageable spotted fever group rickettsiosis. Empiric doxycycline started on clinical/epidemiological grounds (eschar + acral rash + tick exposure) without waiting for confirmatory serology; response is expected within 48 hours.
contraindications: Use with caution in pregnancy (doxycycline still preferred in severe/confirmed rickettsial disease per WHO/ICMR as benefit outweighs risk)
edgeCases: Eschar is often single and painless and is easily missed in skin folds, groin, axilla or scalp
Weil-Felis is insensitive early; a negative early serology does not exclude the diagnosis
Acral rash involving palms/soles and an eschar favour spotted fever group over scrub typhus and over dengue
expectedMaiK: Early, mild spotted fever group rickettsiosis identified from the triad of an eschar, an acral (wrists/ankles/palms) maculopapular rash and rural tick exposure; start empiric doxycycline promptly rather than awaiting confirmatory serology.
expectedNextQuestions: Any tick or dog/livestock contact and search for an overlooked eschar in skin folds?
Distribution and progression of the rash, including palms and soles?
Any bleeding, breathlessness, reduced urine output or confusion to flag early organ dysfunction?
expectedInvestigations: Spotted Fever Group Rickettsia IgM ELISA / paired IFA serology
Malaria smear/RDT and dengue NS1/IgM to exclude mimics

investigations: Spotted Fever Group Rickettsia IgM ELISA / paired IFA serology

regressionAssertions: SCRUB_TYPHUS must appear in the differential
